findings.summary: Pagination cursor's createdAt/id (client-decoded, only type-checked as `string`) are interpolated unescaped into a PostgREST `.or()` filter string (also duplicated server-side at src/dal/notifications.ts:95-96). A crafted cursor containing `,` or `)` could break out of the intended `and(...)` group and add arbitrary OR'd filter clauses. Impact is bounded — RLS (`user_id = auth.uid()`, confirmed live) still governs row visibility regardless of the filter shape, so this cannot leak another user's data, only affects the caller's own query correctness.

senderName/actorName (sourced from users.full_name or the free-text kudos.anonymous_name, which create-kudo.ts only `.trim()`s — no character restriction, confirmed in src/app/(public)/kudos/_actions/create-kudo.ts:152) is substituted into the message template BEFORE `<link>` and `**bold**` markers are parsed. A sender who sets an anonymous nickname containing `**` or `<link>...</link>` gets that markup rendered in the recipient's notification (fake bold text or a fake underlined link). Not exploitable for XSS or open-redirect — the link's `href` is hardcoded to ROUTES.STANDARDS regardless of the injected text (src/app/_components/notifications/notification-item.tsx:96) — but it is a real, demonstrable content-integrity gap at a system boundary (user-controlled free text) that the spec's marker convention did not anticipate.

`/profile` still builds its own role + unreadCount read by hand instead of calling the shared `getViewer()` helper the other 3 screens use — pre-existing duplication (not introduced by this PR) that this PR extends by one more duplicated `getUnreadCount` call. Already tracked as debt in plans/action-items.md per the delivery-tracker report; scoped out of this PR deliberately to keep the diff to notifications.
